prior_scan_disposition.note: Scan-009 covered 4f4d580; 98 files changed since then, mostly prior-scan remediations and glossary count syncs. This scan targets 5 newly added ICESCR article-by-article blog posts not covered by any previous scan.

findings.description: Claim '160 million Americans receive insurance through employer-sponsored plans' stated without citation. Post's own epistemic flags (line 94) acknowledge the figure comes from 'pre-2026 estimates' but body text provides no source.
findings.suggestion: Add inline citation (e.g., Kaiser Family Foundation, 2024; or Census Bureau current population survey) or qualify with 'according to [source].'
findings.context: Approximately 160 million Americans receive insurance through employer-sponsored plans.

findings.description: Claims about 'increased depression rates, elevated substance use, reduced life expectancy in affected cohorts' from prior automation waves stated without any citation. Post's own epistemic flags (line 95) acknowledge 'specific studies not cited.' Claims about reduced life expectancy require sourcing.
findings.suggestion: Cite at least one primary source (e.g., Case & Deaton, 2015 for mortality; Pierce & Schott, 2020 for trade-shock health effects) or reframe as 'multiple researchers have documented...'
findings.context: Research on prior automation waves suggests elevated mental health effects among displaced workers: increased depression rates, elevated substance use, reduced life expectancy in affected cohorts.

findings.description: States '173 other countries' as ICESCR ratifying states count. OHCHR treaty body database shows 171 states parties as of early 2025. Inaccurate treaty-body statistics undermine credibility on an advocacy site.
findings.suggestion: Verify current count against OHCHR status page (https://treaties.un.org) and update. If exact count uncertain at publication time, use hedged form ('over 170 countries').
findings.context: workers in 173 other countries can invoke

findings.description: Scale claim 'the millions of workers' in algorithmically managed roles stated without citation. Post's own epistemic flags identify this as a scope claim without a specific cited source. Self-identified fair-witness gaps that remain in published text represent unresolved quality debt.
findings.suggestion: Add citation (e.g., Mateescu & Nguyen, Data & Society, 2019; or Bureau of Labor Statistics data on electronic monitoring) or soften to 'a large and growing number of workers.'
findings.context: the millions of workers who still have jobs, but whose working conditions now run through software they cannot see

findings.description: Parenthetical citation '(McKinsey Global Institute, 2023; Goldman Sachs, 2023; Acemoglu & Restrepo, 2020)' lacks report titles or page references. Bare institutional names without report titles make verification difficult for readers.
findings.suggestion: Add report titles: e.g., 'McKinsey Global Institute, The Economic Potential of Generative AI, 2023' and 'Goldman Sachs, The Potentially Large Effects of AI on Economic Growth, 2023.'
findings.context: Research suggests AI automation could affect a substantial share of current work activities within a decade (McKinsey Global Institute, 2023; Goldman Sachs, 2023; Acemoglu & Restrepo, 2020)

findings.description: E-Prime violation in author's own prose: 'health facilities and services must be affordable for all' — 'must be' represents a form of 'to be' where an active verb serves equally well. Not a direct treaty quotation (the sentence paraphrases GC 14).
findings.suggestion: Rephrase to 'the framework mandates affordability for all' or 'the framework requires that health facilities and services remain affordable for all.'
findings.context: Economic accessibility receives explicit treatment — health facilities and services must be affordable for all, including socially disadvantaged groups.

findings.description: Internal link '(/2026-04-22-article-14-compulsory-primary-education)' uses bare slug format. If the site's blog routing expects a '/posts/' prefix or date-based path structure, this link will 404. Other internal links in the series use established paths ('/action/', '/tags/icescr/').
findings.suggestion: Verify the link resolves in the built site. If the blog framework routes via '/posts/[slug]/' or strips the date prefix, update the href accordingly.

epistemic_flags: ICESCR ratification count (f3): 171 reflects knowledge-base state as of early 2025; verify against current OHCHR data before treating as authoritative
E-Prime finding (f6) borderline — 'must be' in paraphrased treaty language sits at the boundary between author prose and source material
